scope: Deep-dossier enrichment of the published Dominion Dynamics, CAE, and Lockheed Martin Canada records, emphasizing concrete technologies, current Canadian programs, durable government corroboration, and stable-ID refresh operations.

prospects.name: Dominion Dynamics
prospects.fitSummary: The existing published organization is the intended target; current official AURION evidence adds material product-scale and government-relationship details absent from its capability record.

recoveryAttempts.outcome: The official product page resolves AURION's current data scale, procurement-chain, lobbying, funding, supplier-registry, opportunity, and department analysis functions.
Global Affairs Canada independently resolves founder identity and Dominion as a Canadian defence-technology company focused on sovereign aerospace, autonomy, and command and control.
The live service corroborates that AURION is operational and exposes searchable procurement, opportunity, organization, and entity views rather than being announcement-only.

prospects.name: CAE
prospects.fitSummary: The published CAE profile omits its concrete MAD-XR magnetic-anomaly-detection technology and does not separately represent its Government of Canada Future Fighter Lead-in Training role.

recoveryAttempts.outcome: CAE's official product page documents the compact digital MAD-XR sensor, submarine-detection role, reduced size, weight and power, and use across fixed-wing, rotary-wing and remotely piloted platforms.
The live government program page names CAE as strategic partner to DND and the RCAF for development of Future Fighter Lead-in Training.
The government award announcement corroborates CAE's role, sovereign fighter-training outcome, employment scope, and relationship to CF-35A transition.

prospects.name: Lockheed Martin Canada
prospects.fitSummary: The published profile omits current Canadian Coast Guard information and science-management systems and does not separately represent the renewed Halifax-class combat-system sustainment program.

recoveryAttempts.outcome: The official feature resolves Lockheed Martin Canada's Coast Guard Information System and Science Management System role for AOPS Coast Guard variants 7 and 8.

The official program account describes the CSI ISS award through 2045, more than 160 Canadian personnel, CMS 330 software releases, systems engineering, integration, training, and embedded fleet support.
Public Services and Procurement Canada independently confirms the Lockheed Martin Canada CSI ISS award, Halifax-class scope, and value up to C$1.85 billion.
